Unknown members, missing members, duplicate member names at any object level, non-string text values, an empty old_text, and an empty edits array are invalid. JSON escape spelling has no semantic effect after decoding. Every string consists only of Unicode scalar values, contains no NUL, satisfies its applicable Section 13 predicate and configured limit, and, for path, also satisfies Section 14.

A verified freeform codec carries only the decoded patch string. Its complete transport payload is strict UTF-8 without a BOM. After transport decoding, JSON and freeform inputs canonicalize to the same UTF-8 scalar sequence or are rejected.

The patch document is a sequence of records separated uniformly by LF or uniformly by CRLF. Bare CR and mixed record separators are invalid. The final *** End Patch record MAY be followed by exactly one record separator; every other record MUST be terminated. There are no ignorable blank records, comments, escapes, indentation, or trailing spaces on control records.

BEGIN = "*** Begin Patch v1" END = "*** End Patch" ADD = "*** Add File: " PATH UPDATE = "*** Update File: " PATH MOVE = "*** Move to: " PATH DELETE = "*** Delete File: " PATH HUNK = "@@" | "@@ " LABEL CONTEXT = " " PAYLOAD REMOVE = "-" PAYLOAD ADD_CONTENT = "+" PAYLOAD NO_NEWLINE = "\ No newline at end of file" EOF_ANCHOR = "*** End of File"

Quoted text denotes exact code points. PATH is the non-empty remainder of its record and is valid only under Section 14; there is no quoting or unescaping. LABEL is a non-empty sequence of Unicode scalar values other than CR, LF, NUL, control, or bidirectional-control characters, with no leading or trailing whitespace. It is display-only and never matching authority. PAYLOAD is zero or more Unicode scalar values other than CR, LF, NUL, or an unpaired surrogate. A blank content line is therefore represented by its one prefix character. Content that resembles a control record remains content because it has a context, remove, or add prefix.

The first record MUST be BEGIN; the last semantic record MUST be END. There MUST be one or more file declarations between them. Any unrecognized record, BEGIN or END in another position, or control record in a state not allowed below invalidates the complete request.

Canonical patch-document bytes are strict UTF-8 without a BOM, with every record separator normalized to LF and exactly one LF after END. No Unicode normalization is performed. These bytes, together with the tool and grammar versions, feed the canonical request digest.

An add declaration begins with ADD. Its body consists of zero or more consecutive ADD_CONTENT records followed by at most one NO_NEWLINE, and it ends immediately before the next ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, or END record. Zero content records creates an empty file. Each content record contributes its payload followed by one logical newline, except that NO_NEWLINE MAY occur once, immediately after the final ADD_CONTENT record, to remove that final logical newline. It cannot appear for an empty file or before more content.
A delete declaration is exactly one DELETE record. Its next record MUST be another file header or END.

An update declaration begins with UPDATE. It MAY have exactly one MOVE record immediately after the header. It then contains zero or more hunks. An update without MOVE MUST contain at least one hunk; an update with MOVE and no hunks is a move-only declaration.

Each hunk begins with HUNK and contains context, remove, and add-content records plus only the two special records allowed below. It ends immediately before the next HUNK, file header, or END. A hunk MUST contain at least one REMOVE or ADD_CONTENT; context-only and empty hunks are invalid. The old side is the ordered sequence of CONTEXT and REMOVE payloads. The new side is the ordered sequence of CONTEXT and ADD_CONTENT payloads. A normal body record contributes its payload followed by a logical newline to its applicable side.

NO_NEWLINE MAY immediately follow a REMOVE, ADD_CONTENT, or CONTEXT record. It attaches to the preceding record's old side, new side, or both sides respectively, removes the applicable logical newline, and MAY appear at most once per side in a hunk. No later body record may contribute to a side to which it attached. A hunk containing NO_NEWLINE MUST end with EOF_ANCHOR.

EOF_ANCHOR MAY appear exactly once and only as the final record of a hunk. It asserts that the hunk's old-side match ends at exact logical EOF. When the old side is empty, the declaration input MUST be an empty file; the anchor selects its single insertion point and the hunk MUST contain at least one ADD_CONTENT record. A nonempty input requires explicit old context. This is the only context-free pure insertion. It is not a fuzzy anchor.

Without EOF_ANCHOR, the old side MUST be non-empty. With or without the anchor, Section 11.3 unique matching, same-snapshot resolution, range non-overlap, and Section 13 representation rules apply. Only an EOF-anchored hunk can change final-newline state. NO_NEWLINE controls only whether its attached hunk-side record contributes a logical newline; the planner computes the complete proposed bytes and derives final-newline change by comparing the full pre- and post-file states. Marker presence or parity alone is not authoritative, especially when a side is empty. A non-EOF update preserves final-newline state.
Declaration order is semantic, but the global transition ledger in Section 12 controls reuse and conflicts. Duplicate headers do not merge implicitly.
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Add File: empty.txt *** End Patch
A one-line file without a final newline is valid:
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Add File: note.txt +hello \ No newline at end of file *** End Patch
Insertion into an empty existing file is valid:
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Update File: empty.txt @@ +hello \ No newline at end of file *** End of File *** End Patch

Given log.txt with exact content base
, appending a newline-terminated line is valid and produces base
x
:
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Update File: log.txt @@ base +x *** End of File *** End Patch
Given log.txt with exact content base and no final newline, appending a line while retaining no final newline is valid and produces base\nx:
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Update File: log.txt @@ -base \ No newline at end of file +base +x \ No newline at end of file *** End of File *** End Patch
*** Begin Patch v1 *** Update File: old/name.txt *** Move to: new/name.txt *** End Patch

The following are invalid: an unversioned or unknown begin marker; an empty record between declarations; whitespace after a control record; an unprefixed content line; a move record anywhere except immediately after its update header; a delete body; a context-only hunk; a context-free insertion without EOF_ANCHOR; an empty-old-side EOF insertion into a nonempty file; an unattached or non-final NO_NEWLINE; a second marker for one side; content after that side's marker; an EOF anchor not last in its hunk; a mixed-separator document; an unknown or duplicate JSON member; and any path or operation chain denied elsewhere in this specification.
